Description:
The same inner tangential contact as EqualCylindersCrossedAtSeam, but placed where nothing is special:
two cylinders of equal radius 10 whose axes cross at 55 degrees, in a direction that has nothing to do
with the coordinate planes.
cylA is the cylinder about the z axis. cylB is a copy of it, rotated by 55 degrees about the axis
  u = (-sin 33, cos 33, 0) = (-0.5446390350, 0.8386705679, 0)
through the origin, so its axis points along (0.6869987103, 0.4461421789, 0.5735764364).
u is perpendicular to both cylinder axes, so the two mantles are tangent to each other at
  +-10*u = (-5.4463903502, 8.3867056795, 0) and (5.4463903502, -8.3867056795, 0)
and the intersection curve - two ellipses again, as for any two equal cylinders with crossing axes -
has a NODE at each of them.

The azimuth 33 degrees is the point of the case: the two nodes sit at 123 and 303 degrees on the mantle
of cylA, that is in the INTERIOR of its two half mantle faces, far from the seams at 0 and 180 degrees,
and at 123 degrees away from cylB's seam as well - the rotation carries the seam along and it fixes u.
So the same degeneracy has to be found without any face boundary, pole or symmetry plane to hint at it.

The rotation by 55 degrees about u is not an involution, but the configuration is still symmetric: the
rotation by 180 degrees about the bisector of the two axes exchanges cylA and cylB, so the two
differences must be congruent and must measure the same.

cylA is deliberately ASYMMETRIC about the contact plane, z from -40 to 55. That changes nothing about
the contact - the intersection body stays inside |z| <= 19.21 - but it makes the two halves each
difference falls into differ in volume. With a symmetric cylinder those halves are congruent and their
canonical order is then decided by a volume difference of 7e-7 relative, which is not a sound basis for
a recorded extent.
Expected:
V(cylinder r=10, l=95) = pi*100*95 = 29845.1302091030 for both operands, area 2*pi*10*95 + 2*pi*100 =
6597.3445725386, edgeLength 4*pi*10 + 2*95 = 315.6637061436.

The intersection of two infinite cylinders of equal radius r whose axes cross at the angle theta is
known in closed form:
  V = 16*r^3/(3*sin theta) = 16000/(3*sin 55) = 6510.7978067278
The cylinders are long enough for that to apply unchanged: the intersection body reaches only
|z| = 19.21 along the axis of cylA, well inside it, so no cap takes part. Checked by Monte Carlo over
the box 20x20x60: 6509.6 +- 5.3 (4e6 samples), 0.2 sigma from the closed form.

Hence, exactly:
  union       2*29845.1302091030 - 6510.7978067278 = 53179.4626114783
  difference  29845.1302091030 - 6510.7978067278   = 23334.3324023753, the same for both ways round
Each difference is a cylinder with an oblique cylindrical hole of its own diameter through it. As in
EqualCylindersCrossedAtSeam the hole removes a full cross section - at z = 0 the whole disc of cylA is
inside cylB and touches its mantle only at the two nodes - so the body falls into two halves that hang
together at those two points alone:
  pi*100*40 - 6510.7978067278/2 =  9310.9717109953   and   pi*100*55 - 3255.3989033639 = 14023.3606913800

The intersection is one solid bounded by four cylindrical faces meeting at the two nodes: 4 faces,
4 edges, 2 vertices, and not a single planar face.
Status:
REGRESSED on 2026-08-28 by the second fix of that day, and this is the one case of the group that got
WORSE rather than better. It passed with a recorded baseline before; now the face partition varies
between runs, a regenerate run refuses to write, and the case is left unpinned.

THE GEOMETRY IS STILL RIGHT. No run differs in volume, and the values match the same closed forms as
before:
  obliqueInter   against 16*r^3/(3*sin 55) = 6510.7978067278
  obliqueUnion   against 2*29845.1302091030 - 6510.7978067278 = 53179.4626114783
  the halves     against 14023.3606913800 and 9310.9717109953
  the two differences against each other, congruent by the 180 degree rotation about the bisector
What varies over 4 runs is only how the result is cut into faces:
  obliqueInter          10 edges and 6 vertices, or 9 and 5 (edgeLength 210.484 or 210.601)
  obliqueBminusA#0/#1   4 faces or 5, with a seam edge of 20.52 moving from the one part to the other
                        (edgeLength 257.700/207.180 in one run, 237.180/227.700 in another)
That is exactly the failure mode the same fix REMOVED from ConesCommonInsphereAtSeam,
ConeCylinderCommonInsphere, TorusVillarceauPlaneAtSeam, TorusVillarceauPlaneOblique and
TorusSphereSaddleAtSeam - five cases that could not be pinned before and can be now. Here it appeared
for the first time. The seam version of the same contact, EqualCylindersCrossedAtSeam, stayed stable,
so whatever decides it is not the tangential contact alone.

THE BASELINE THAT WAS LOST is in the git history of this file: obliqueInter had 4 faces, 4 edges and 2
vertices - the two vertices being the two tangential nodes and no planar face at all, which is the
tidiest partition this body can have. It is worth getting back to.

WHY THERE IS NO BASELINE: a regenerate run executes the case 4 times and refuses to write when the runs
disagree; pinning one of several outcomes would only produce noise. Once the partition is deterministic
again, record with Regenerate and set CaseStatus back to Ok.
